subject: RLHF workload: Dedicated SKU options and memory-tiling plan

Subject: Dedicated capacity for RLHF-heavy endpoints

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latencies looked promising. We're starting to map out required Dedicated capacity for a pilot: our RLHF scoring and preference model will run a mix of long-rollout decoding (8k tokens typical, peaks to 16k), per-request context caching, and frequent small-batch fine-tuning jobs.

Two asks to help us scope a committed capacity proposal:
- A short write-up on H100 vs A100 vs L4 for this workload (memory vs throughput vs cost tradeoffs).
- A suggested reserve mix and fallback policy if peak long-context requests spike (we need an ops-safe plan for production).

I've attached a CSV with sample traffic shapes and some token-level cost targets.

Appreciate a quick first-pass this week — we have an internal procurement window in two weeks.

Cheers,
Alex
Founder, Orbital AI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for RLHF-heavy endpoints

Alex — thanks for the dataset. Quick summary up front, then a proposed next step.

High-level guidance (short version):
- H100: best for peak long-context decoding and throughput-sensitive RLHF runs. Higher perf for fp16/amp and attention kernels; we prefer it for sustained sampling that touches large KV caches (80GB HBM variant helps avoid spillage).
- A100 (80GB): good middle-ground when you need native memory headroom but want lower per-unit cost than H100 for some batched offline training/fine-tune steps. Slightly older kernel optimizations but stable.
- L4 (24GB): cost-efficient for short-context, small-batch scoring and embeddings. Not ideal as primary for 8k+ streams unless heavily quantized and sharded; good for burst/offload tiers.

Recommended immediate action: 45-minute alignment call with Jordan + Irene so we can map your samples to a concrete reserve plan (H100 vs A100 slots + L4 burst). I'll sketch a draft reserve mix and an ops fallback policy after that call.

Provisional concerns:
- Model memory growth during sampling: attention cache and intermediate activations will push effective memory above static model weights for very long contexts.
- Prefetching/tiling: we may need prefix-KV tiling and smart eviction to keep p99 latency within SLOs.

I'll drop a short technical note (ops-focused) to the thread with initial numeric tradeoffs.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for RLHF-heavy endpoints

Alex / team — adding ops context from the runtime side. Irene and I did a quick pass on the CSV. Key observations:

1) Effective working set size matters more than static model size.
   - Example: 8k tokens with 2 KV layers and a 70B model can require ~1.4–2.0x model-weight memory when accounting for KV + activations during sampling.

2) H100 benefits:
   - HBM3 bandwidth and transformer kernel optimizations reduce p50/p95 generation latency for long sequences.
   - Better for continuous-batching under high concurrency; fewer context evictions.

3) A100 benefits:
   - 80GB A100 gives comfortable headroom for long contexts with slightly lower unit cost. Good if you expect mixed offline fine-tune work on the same pool.

4) L4 notes:
   - Best as a secondary tier: cheap scoring/embeddings and short-step policy-model calls. With int8 quant and KV caching you can push to ~6–8k in constrained cases, but expect higher variance.

Draft reserve mix (pilot): 
- 40% H100 (p95 long-context endpoints + canary RLHF scoring)
- 40% A100 (background training/fine-tune + moderate-length endpoints)
- 20% L4 (scoring, embeddings, burst offload)

Fallback policy (ops-safe):
- If H100 pool utilization > 85% sustained (10m rolling): route new long-context requests to A100 with early-stopping policy or to a degraded L4 path (lower precision) with informative headers to the app.
- Pre-configure graceful degradation: prefer throughput-preserving degradation (smaller beam/early stop) over hard rejects.

Irene, can you add expected slot counts and a quick cost delta?

—Jordan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for RLHF-heavy endpoints — pilot sizing (numbers)

Team / Alex — quick numbers based on the CSV and our empirical perf profiles. Assumptions: 70B base model, fp16 decoding, average request 8k tokens, peak concurrency 120 simultaneous decodes, typical batch efficiency 1.8x with continuous batching.

Estimated slot needs (pilot, 99th percentile coverage):
- H100 (80GB): 12 slots — covers ~48 concurrent long-context decodes assuming ~4 decodes per GPU at target latency with continuous batching.
- A100 (80GB): 10 slots — covers mixed workload: 30 long-ish decodes + background ft jobs (tradeoff by scheduling).
- L4 (24GB): 8 slots — used for scoring, embeddings, and best-effort degraded long-contexts with int8.

Cost delta (monthly, rough):
- H100 pool (12 slots): ~$190k/mo (reserve pricing estimate)
- A100 pool (10 slots): ~$120k/mo
- L4 pool (8 slots): ~$14k/mo
- Combined pilot reserve: ~$324k/mo (before committed-discount negotiation)

Operational policies to include in the deal:
- KV prefetching enabled per-route with per-customer cache caps to avoid cross-customer blowups.
- Canary lane on H100: 2 slots reserved for canary rollouts and perf testing.
- Auto-fallback thresholds (as Jordan outlined) and telemetry hooks (token-level traces + per-request memory usage).

Next step: Alex — if this fits procurement bandwidth, we can map to a 6-week pilot commit and a 3-month follow-up sizing review.

Thanks,
Irene

Thanks — this is super helpful and clearer than our internal model. A couple clarifying Qs before we take to procurement:
1) You recommend H100 for p95 long-context. If we negotiated a slightly lower H100 count but larger A100 pool, what runtime behaviors should we expect (latency / p95 impact)?
2) For the L4 fallback, what level of dequantization/quality drop do you expect when we switch to int8 degraded path? Any recommended automatic signals we should expose to product so they can gracefully degrade UI?

We want to avoid a hard band where user experience suddenly collapses. If you have a short blurb we can copy into our SRE runbook that lists recommended product-visible signals (e.g., confidence score, token-per-second drop, early-stop flag) that would be great.

—Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@orbitalai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya@orbitalai.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for RLHF-heavy endpoints — pilot sizing (numbers)

Alex — answers inline + a copyable SRE blurb at the bottom.

1) Fewer H100, more A100: expected behavior
- Latency: p50 largely unchanged; p95 will increase for very long contexts because A100 has slightly higher per-token time for the big-attention kernels on Hopper-optimized models. Expect p95 delta of ~10–30% depending on request mix.
- Throughput: A100 can sustain decent batch throughput but will show higher variance under many concurrent 16k requests. You can partially mitigate by raising continuous-batching windows (cost vs latency trade).

2) L4 int8 fallback quality drop
- Typical quality regression for generative RLHF-style scoring when moving to int8: small but measurable — lower coherence on long-rollout completion and occasional token hallucination edges. For preference scoring, int8 tends to preserve relative ordering fairly well if you calibrate with a small validation set.

SRE runbook blurb (copy into your docs):
"Degraded-inference signals and recommended product actions:
- Confidence Delta: expose per-response confidence or score delta; if confidence drops > 8% vs route baseline, surface a subtle UX note ("quality-limited mode").
- Token/sec drop: if per-request token/sec falls below 60% of baseline for the route, route to a higher-tier path or show progress indicator with early-stop option.
- Early-stop flag: allow model to emit an early_stop hint when it has hit a soft budget; product should present a compact completion and optional "continue" button.
- Telemetry: record memory usage and fallback reason in the same trace for postmortems.
"

Next steps: if you approve the pilot mix and cost, I'll get a procurement-facing summary and proposed legal SOW for a 6-week pilot.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
